extracted.intended_audience: HUD Field Offices, HUD grant recipients, State and local governments and practitioners responsible for implementing HUD environmental review and floodplain/wetlands compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the criteria, standards, and exceptions in HUD's proposed 24 CFR part 55 implementing Executive Orders 11988 and 11990 for floodplain management and wetland protection, aimed at HUD staff, grant recipients, and local/state entities carrying out environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum documentation requirements (§55.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 55.27 clarifies the minimum documentation requirements for HUD Field Offices or grant recipients for compliance under §§ 55.20, 55.24, 55.25, or 55.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulated information collection burden: e.g., Documentation of compliance by grant recipients subject to 24 CFR part 58 (55.27) — estimated 3,200 respondents, 1 response each, 0.4 hours per response, total 1,280 hours. Documentation is required to demonstrate compliance with the decisionmaking/avoidance/mitigation requirements of part 55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of Subpart C where no functional purpose served
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will exclude certain program activities from the Subpart C decisionmaking process where 'no functional purpose would be served' by carrying out subpart C procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD criteria for exclusion include: (1) activities controlled sufficiently under FEMA's NFIP regulatory structure; (2) activities that do not have direct or indirect development impact on floodplains or wetlands (involve no locational decision involving a floodplain or wetland); or (3) activities with de minimis development impact on floodplains or wetlands. HUD also considers practicable alternatives and whether there exists practicable means of further minimizing impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion rationale for HUD financial assistance for existing one- to four-family properties
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD proposes excluding mortgage insurance actions on existing one- to four-family properties in FEMA-designated floodplain zones from Subpart C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary rationales: (1) FHA financing decisions (purchase, mortgage, refinance) involve no practicable locational alternative for the owner; (2) such HUD financial assistance has de minimis direct or indirect development impacts; (3) procedural avoidance under EO 11988 would serve no functional purpose. Where community is in good standing under NFIP, later substantial improvements must meet NFIP hazard minimization requirements (44 CFR 60.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of HUD-acquired one- to four-family properties — limited Subpart C applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of HUD-acquired one- to four-family properties in floodplains proposed to be excluded from the Subpart C decisionmaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although disposition program would be subject to documentation/notification requirements in proposed §55.22, HUD proposes exclusion because avoidance requirement is impossible (no practicable alternatives to location of the HUD-acquired property). Exclusion applies only to properties in communities in good standing with the NFIP. Any substantial improvement remains subject to NFIP hazard minimization rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited applicability for certain disposition activities (multifamily and bulk sales)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD determined that for disposition of HUD-acquired multifamily housing projects and 'bulk sales' of HUD-acquired one- to four-family properties, three of the eight Agency review requirements under proposed §55.20 would not serve a functional purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD recognizes structural program reasons that make some of the §55.20 review steps unnecessary for these disposition types; nonetheless other documentation/notification requirements may still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 223(f) mortgage insurance program exemptions and four-step procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD proposes to exempt the section 223(f) program from three requirements in the Executive Orders (proposed §55.20(b), (c), and (g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD established a four-step procedure for the 223(f) program: Identification of Floodplain Location, Impact Determination, Mitigation Considerations, and Decision. This procedure is intended to meet the intent of EO 11988 and achieve compliance with the remaining applicable steps under the proposed regulation. Rehabilitation financed under section 223(f) must be less than thresholds for 'substantial rehabilitation' under 24 CFR 225.3(I) and 255.201.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability where HUD program activities have no direct or indirect development impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD actions that do not have direct or indirect development impacts (and involve no locational decision) do not require formal compliance with part 55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: (i) HUD-assisted exempt activities in 24 CFR 58.34; (ii) policy-level actions in 24 CFR 50.16 not involving site-based decisions; (iii) HUD implementation of Interstate Land Sales Disclosure Act registration/disclosure; (iv) GNMA secondary mortgage operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis development impact exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions having de minimis direct or indirect development impacts may be excluded from Subpart C and, in some cases, from part 55 as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (i) Financial assistance for minor repairs/improvements on one- to four-family properties not meeting thresholds for 'substantial' work; (ii) minor amendments to previously approved actions with no additional adverse impact; (iii) approval of a project site with an incidental portion in a wetland/floodplain only if (A) construction/landscaping do not occupy/modify wetland or floodplain (except minor grubbing/clearing/pruning/sodding/seeding), (B) appropriate provision for site drainage, and (C) covenant or comparable restriction to preserve floodplain/wetland; (iv) issuance/use of Housing Vouchers/Section 8 Certificates/unit-based rental subsidies (non-project-based).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other specific exclusions where formal compliance serves no functional purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD lists other program activities for which formal compliance with part 55 would serve no functional purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (i) repossession/receivership/foreclosure actions to protect HUD's financial interests under existing loans/grants/mortgage insurance; (ii) interim/emergency activities involving imminent threats to health/safety limited to necessary protection/repair/restoration; (iii) HUD approval where FEMA has issued a final or conditional Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) removing or conditionally removing property from FEMA-designated floodplain (FEMA remains lead agency for EO compliance); (iv) HUD acceptance of housing subdivision approvals by VA or Farmers Home Administration where HUD may rely on their compliance; (v) actions already approved and ongoing as of effective date (no new reviewable action), provided any prior required hazard minimization measures are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of HUD MPS §200.926d(c)(4) — 100-year base flood standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision replaces 50-year base flood standard for basements in §200.926d(c)(4)(i) with a 100-year floodplain standard to conform with FEMA's NFIP regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: consistency with NFIP and Flood Disaster Protection Act; reduce HUD insurance fund exposure. Proposed §200.926d(c)(4)(i)-(v) would recognize FEMA variances and exceptions (44 CFR 60.3 and §60.6). HUD requests comments on clarifying application of NFIP regulations and supplementing FEMA for 'critical actions', structures without basements, and coastal high hazard areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for residential structures with basements
rubrics_metrics.description: The elevation of the lowest floor (basement) in structures with basements would be at or above the runoff and base flood level (100-year flood level) required for new construction or substantial improvement under FEMA NFIP regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variance and exception procedures under NFIP would be incorporated by reference for compliance. HUD requests comment from agencies and industry experts on application and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for residential structures without basements
rubrics_metrics.description: First floors of structures without basements would be at or above the FEMA-designated base flood elevation (100-year recurrence flood elevation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard aligns HUD-required elevations with FEMA NFIP base flood elevations for new construction or substantial improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for non-'critical actions' in coastal high hazard areas
rubrics_metrics.description: For HUD proposed actions not meeting the 'critical action' definition but located in FEMA-designated 'coastal high hazard areas', basements or any permanent enclosure of space below the lowest floor would be prohibited, and underside of the lowest floor and its horizontal supports would be at or above the FEMA-designated base flood level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: provides necessary margin of safety against tidal/wave/rapid saltwater damage and structural deterioration. Applies to areas designated Zone V, VE, or V on FIRMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate elevation standard (one foot above base flood)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed alternate standard (not set in rule) would require: (1) lowest floor elevation of one- and two-family residential structures without basements be at or above one foot above FEMA base flood elevation; and (2) underside of lowest floor and horizontal supports in coastal high hazard areas be at least one foot above base flood level where FEMA has determined without establishing stillwater elevations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD solicits comment on empirical evidence and cost-benefit tradeoffs. Example cost calculation provided: fill costs, finance charges, and estimated annual insurance premium savings demonstrating potential net homeowner savings over mortgage life. HUD asks whether 'fill' is the only cost or if other costs (welded wire fabric, extra concrete/labor) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for 'critical actions'
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed HUD 'critical actions' (defined in §55.2(b)(2)), the lowest floor of a structure, including basements and all mechanical, electrical, and service equipment, would be at or above the FEMA-designated 500-year frequency flood elevation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Critical actions' would be prohibited in FEMA-designated 'floodways' and 'coastal high hazard areas'. Typical critical actions include hospitals, nursing homes, convalescent homes, intermediate care facilities, board and care facilities, and retirement service centers. All critical actions must be designed or modified to include: (1) preparation of and participation in an early warning system; (2) an emergency evacuation and relocation plan; (3) identification of evacuation route(s) out of the 500-year floodplain; and (4) identification marks of past or estimated flood levels on all structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions in §55.1(c) (actions not approvable after effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for actions listed in §55.12(c), no HUD financial assistance may be approved after the effective date for: (1) any action located in a floodway (other than functionally dependent use); (2) any critical action located in a coastal high hazard area; or (3) any non-critical action located in a coastal high hazard area unless the action is designed for location in such area or is functionally dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An action 'designed for location' in a coastal high hazard area means: for new construction/substantial rehabilitation, the work meets current FEMA V zone standards (44 CFR 60.3(e)) and applicable HUD MPS; for existing construction, the work either met FEMA elevation/construction standards applicable when originally constructed or would meet at least the earliest FEMA standards for construction in the 100-year floodplain if constructed before FEMA standards became effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified definitions: 'coastal high hazard area' and 'critical action'
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions modified for part 55: 'Coastal high hazard area' means area subject to high velocity waters (hurricane wave wash or tsunamis) designated on FIRM as Zone V1-30, VE, or V. 'Critical action' means any activity for which even a slight chance of flooding would be too great because flooding might cause loss of life, injury, or property damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Floodplain delineation will rely on FIRMs and FHBMs; FEMA zones also relied on for '100-year' and '500-year' floodplain and 'floodway' delineations. Critical actions include facilities producing/storing highly hazardous materials or facilities serving vulnerable populations (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives to full duplicate review — aggregation, areawide compliance, adoption of another agency's review
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 55 provides certain cost-effective alternatives (e.g., aggregation and areawide compliance) for HUD and grantee implementation of the Executive Orders and allows adoption of another agency's review under the Executive Orders (proposed §55.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mechanisms are intended to minimize regulatory burden and avoid duplication of evaluation efforts when another Federal agency or grant recipient has already evaluated applicable Executive Order requirements; HUD may rely on FEMA NFIP regulations or another agency's compliance record where appropriate, subject to documentation requirements.
